Marcus came off the wharf with the wind still in his coat and the salt not yet dry upon his hands. The harbor was quiet in the wrong way, with ropes knocking lightly and no one willing to say why the late packet had missed the tide. Men glanced at one another and kept their business moving. That was how fear walked in a port that meant to earn its supper. Marcus asked for the tally book, found the figures neat, and trusted them less for it. A clean account can be an honest thing, but it can also be the mark left by a liar with time to spare. He looked down the line of crates, counted them again, and heard behind him the scrape of a boot that stopped a little too suddenly. By then he knew that whatever was missing had not gone far.
